name: University of Inland Norway (INN)
summary: University with campuses across inland Norway; its Game School in Hamar teaches two English bachelor's, in game art and animation and game technology.

ib.text: The IB Diploma, with English, meets the entry requirement; Norwegian is not required for either game degree. With a Nordic school background you apply through Samordna opptak.

apply.via: INN's own application, or Samordna opptak (Nordic schooling)

dates.label: Application opens for EU/EEA applicants (yearly date)

programmes.name: Bachelor in Game Art and Animation
programmes.ib: Pass INN's entrance exam, plus an interview if the committee asks. 2026 criteria; 2027 exam dates not yet published.
programmes.about: Art for games made with studio tools, specialising from the second semester as a game animator, 3D artist, 2D concept artist or technical artist, and building real games every semester with the game technology students.
programmes.selectionNote: The entrance exam decides who is qualified; in 2026 every qualified Samordna opptak applicant got an offer. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Bachelor in Game Technology
programmes.ib: Maths at Norwegian R1 level: any IB maths (AA or AI, SL or HL) at grade 3 or better covers it.
programmes.about: Programming for games and interactive media, in teams with artists and designers from the first semester; from year two you specialise in game programming (engines, mechanics, networking) or computer graphics (3D, shaders, simulation).

needs.note: Norwegian R1 level; Samordna opptak accepts AI SL through S1+S2.

programmes.selectionNote: Samordna opptak ranks qualified applicants on school grades; INN does not say how it ranks its own EU/EEA route, and publishes no places or cut-off.

notes: The two game degrees share projects every semester, so artists and programmers build games together.
INN's Philosophy, Politics and Economics bachelor in Lillehammer is taught in Norwegian, not English.
INN sends applicants 'with upper secondary education from the Nordic countries' to Samordna opptak, and an IB from a school in Denmark is upper secondary education in a Nordic country.
